newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset declines third mobile licence bid.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset declines third mobile licence bid.

text.p: Italian opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi and the majority shareholder in TV and media group Mediaset said that Mediaset does not intend to compete for Italy's third mobile phone licence.

He also added that Mediaset does not intend to enter the shareholding of Italy's second mobile phone consortium Omnitel, where the major shareholder is Olivetti. Berlusconi was speaking at a meeting with the foreign reporters.
"I am sure that Mediaset will not participate in the round for the third mobile telephone licence because frankly we have no hope of getting the concession from the government," said Berlusconi.
"I can guarantee that Mediaset has no intention of entering into Omnitel, in the telecoms sector," Berlusconi added.

Mediaset had been believed to be a leading candidate to apply for the third mobile licence through its relationship with Albacom, the joint venture between state-controlled bank BNL and British Telecommunications.
Berlusconi's company Fininvest has a near half share in Mediaset, while he is also leader of the centre-right opposition in Italy's parliament.
The competition for the third mobile licence was scheduled for this year, with the successful bidder set to join other operators -- the state controlled Telecom Italia Mobile TIM) and Omnitel.
